structure: Part 1, Animals journey pages. Read in full: tests/animals/e2e/pages/README.md and the 14 one-page specs for the live-animals journey (origin 7 tests, commodities 7, animal-identification 3, consignment-details 3, import-reason 5, additional-details 3, cph-number 4, arrival-details 7, transited-countries 5, transporter 4, transporter-selection 3, transporter-add 3, contact-address 7, declaration 2: 63 tests in all, every one tagged @integration and @duplicated-in-frontend); the page objects they drive (page-objects/index.ts, shared/base-page.ts, shared/sets.ts, shared/index.ts, animals/index.ts and the 17 animals page objects from origin-of-import to declaration, including commercial- and private-transporter); the UI journey helper flows/animals/journey.ts and flows/shared/journey-context.ts; fixtures/ui.ts and fixtures/index.ts; every file in domain/animals/constants (journey-options, import-reasons, country-codes, point-of-entries, certification-purposes, document-types, commodity-types, means-of-transport, commodity-codes, sort-by-values, animals-dynamics-statuses, commodity-species); domain/shared/constants/yes-no-values.ts; domain/shared/types/date-time-input.ts; utils/date-utils.ts. Claims run page by page in journey order: for each page its route (the page object's slug under /live-animals/notifications/{id}/), heading, fields, options and error strings the page object locates, then one claim per test saying what it proves. After the pages come the journey order and default answers flows/animals/journey.ts walks, the shared chrome base-page.ts locates, the option values in the constants, and the date rules date-utils.ts gives the arrival-details tests. Gaps record validation messages or empty submits the specs leave unasserted.

claims.statement: A new notification is created from the dashboard's create-new-notification button, which lands the user on the Origin of the import page, and the journey id in the URL is used as the notification's reference.

Most tasks on the notification overview are gated behind the origin answer; a brand-new notification's overview entry guard is satisfied by an opening-run marker set at creation rather than by answering origin.

// Origin answered — most other tasks are gated behind it ... // Origin unanswered — the entry guard is satisfied by the opening-run

claims.statement: The commodity section and everything downstream of it is gated behind origin, so a test reaching any page past origin answers origin and the commodity first.
claims.quote:
// The commodity section (and everything downstream) is gated behind origin,
  // so any reach past origin runs unlockSections first.
claims.note: unlockSections() answers the commodity task (answerCommodity), so the helpers also treat the commodity answer as unlocking the later tasks.

claims.quote:
airplane: { value: 'AIRPLANE', display: 'Airplane' },
  railway: { value: 'RAILWAY', display: 'Railway' },
  roadVehicle: { value: 'ROAD_VEHICLE', display: 'Road vehicle' },
  vessel: { value: 'VESSEL', display: 'Vessel' },
claims.note: The UI journey selects the option by the label 'Road Vehicle' (capital V) while this constant displays 'Road vehicle'; the two disagree on the label's case.

claims.statement: Transited countries are needed only when the means of transport is railway or road vehicle.

claims.statement: The full UI journey answers every section in this order: origin (France, region code Yes 75, internal reference Imports456GB), commodity (Bos taurus, 1 animal, 5 packages), identification (ear tag UK123456789012), reason (Internal market, Breeding) and additional details (Slaughter, unweaned No), addresses and CPH (12/345/6789), transport (road vehicle, transited France and Belgium, García Livestock Transport SL), then contact (Animal and Plant Health Agency).

The default test notification shared by the UI journey and the seeder is: country France, commodity Dog, type Domestic, species Bison bison and Bos spp., reason internal market, animals 5 and 19, packages 13 and 21, certification approvedBodies, port Aberdeen Airport, arrival 14 days ahead and means of transport Vessel.
claims.quote:
countryCode: countryCodes.eu.france,
...
  commodityCode: commodityCodes.dog,
  commodityType: commodityTypes.domestic,
  species: [commoditySpecies.bisonBison, commoditySpecies.bosSpp],
  importReason: importReasons.internalMarket,
  noOfAnimals: [5, 19],
  noOfPackages: [13, 21],
  certificationPurpose: certificationPurposes.approvedBodies,
...
  pointOfEntry: pointOfEntries.aberdeen,
  arrivalDate: getRelativeDateInput({ dayOffset: 14 }),
  meansOfTransport: meansOfTransport.vessel,
claims.note: The default pairs a Dog commodity code with cattle species (Bison bison, Bos spp.); the UI journey helper does not use these defaults (it searches Bos taurus).

claims.statement: If sign-in fails, the user sees "Sorry, we are unable to sign you in." with a "try again" link.
After signing in, a user who belongs to more than one organisation is asked to choose an organisation; a user with one organisation never sees that picker.

defra-id-stub shows its "Choose your organisation" picker
   * after sign-in exclusively for those, so single-org identities never hit it.

claims.statement: Opening a notification page while signed out redirects through the sign-in flow (server redirects) before the page is shown.
The suite signs each test worker in once and reuses that session across its tests when session reuse is on.
Calls from the suite that leave CDP for the internet go through the CDP proxy, while journey and service calls go direct.
claims.quote: // Calls that leave CDP for the internet go through its proxy; the journey and service calls stay direct.

claims.statement: Each page spec reaches its page by driving the real UI from the dashboard through the earlier pages, except the declaration spec, which seeds a ready-to-submit draft through the frontend and resumes it in the browser.
